Title: World leaders hope for reset after US midterms
Article:
PARIS: World leaders voiced hopes for a reset with the United States on Wednesday after voters delivered a huge midterm election defeat to President Donald Trump and his Republican party.
The Democrats seized control of both Senate and the House of Representatives, giving them the power to block legislation and hold up Trump's appointments.
Germany
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said he hoped to see new initiatives to end the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.
"With their majority in both chambers of Congress, the Democratic Party will likely seek to shift the political course in the United States," Wadephul said.
Through cooperation between the United States and Europe, "there may be a new opportunity to launch a fresh initiative" to resolve conflicts, he said.
Spain
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Trump's defeat showed that the global far-right was on the wane.
"It happened in Brazil. It just happened in the US. And it will soon happen in Spain," the socialist leader said, with elections looming later this month.
The far-right wave is "no longer growing, it is unravelling," he added.
Russia
Russia hopes Trump will continue his "peacemaking efforts" after the midterm elections, the Kremlin said.
"President Trump continues to exercise his powers. We sincerely hope that he will also continue his peacemaking efforts," spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
South Africa
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the result could thaw strained ties between Pretoria and Washington.
"We're hoping that on a bilateral basis, there will be a coming together of minds where we will find a proper path forward on geopolitics as well as on trade matters and investment matters," he said.
He added that he hoped the result would "introduce a new era in world relations."
EU
The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas voiced hope the new US Congress would support Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia.
"I hope that the new Congress... will continue supporting Ukraine and also putting more pressure on Russia," she said, adding that Europe and the United States "are much stronger together" in pushing Moscow to end its war.
UK
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the result was an opportunity for the world to "unite" around resolving cost-of-living issues.
"President Trump has accepted the results, and I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living," Burnham said.

Title: Sharp metal objects found in Halloween sweets in Austria
Article:
VIENNA:  Austrian police have launched an investigation after small metal objects such as nails, needles and pins were found in Halloween sweets at several locations across the country.
German authorities this week also reported several cases of small metal objects being found inside Halloween sweets.
Austrian police have received 13 reports of metal objects found in sweets collected by children at Halloween, federal criminal police said on Wednesday in a statement sent to AFP.
Although no reported cases have required medical treatment, police urged parents and children to "carefully check... all Halloween sweets before they are eaten."
"Any sweets that have clearly been tampered with must be kept together with their packaging and reported to the police," they said.
Federal police are coordinating an investigation into the incidents, Interior Minister Gerhard Karner and police chief Gerald Tatzgern told a press conference on Tuesday.
The 13 cases have been reported in four provinces, the police said: three in Lower Austria, three in Upper Austria, one in Salzburg and six in Styria.
In Lower Austria, a 10-year-old girl suffered minor injuries to her mouth after biting into a chocolate that had a needle inside, the APA news agency reported.
In Upper Austria, a 28-year-old father in the city of Linz found nails in treats his children had collected and a mother found needles in sweets gathered by her 11-year-old daughter, it said.
Objects found in Styria included a needle, two metal pins and a staple, according to APA.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore toughens haze law, raises maximum fine tenfold to S$20mil
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's parliament passed amendments to the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA), introducing higher maximum fines and stronger investigative and enforcement powers against entities responsible for cross-border haze.
The amendments raise the maximum fine for the main offence tenfold, from S$2million to S$20 million while increasing the daily fine from S$100,000 to S$10million for causing or contributing to land or forest fires that risk causing haze in Singapore.
They also expand investigative powers to trace commercial links and impose restrictions across business arrangements and supply chains to hold entities accountable, while removing legal barriers to enforcement in line with international law.
Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu said the amendments would strengthen Singapore's standing as a jurisdiction with credible and robust environmental standards.
"Transboundary haze is complex, but we are committed to doing what we can within our powers to reduce incentives for unsustainable forestry and agricultural practices.
"The amendments we are making show our commitment to ensuring traceability of our supply chain and curtailing economic benefits of companies engaged in or linked to unlawful practises," she said in her winding-up speech following the parliamentary debate.
Fu said Singapore would continue working with regional partners, including through its role as host of the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre and its 2027 Asean chairmanship, to strengthen the bloc's long-term capacity to tackle transboundary haze.
"The THPA is not a silver bullet, it is one of many tools we must use to address the transboundary haze situation," she added.
Meanwhile, Singapore Institute of International Affairs chairman Simon Tay said the amendments would strengthen penalties against companies responsible for transboundary haze.
"The THPA is a legal weapon that can be used against corporations, it will enable Singapore to act effectively against errant companies," he told Bernama.
However, Tay cautioned that tougher legislation alone could not prevent future haze incidents, particularly amid climate change.
"Cooperation within the Asean framework and with Indonesia and neighbouring countries will also be essential," he added.

Title: UK man tells rape trial he thought snoring woman was 'roleplaying'
Article:
LONDON: A UK man accused of raping a woman whose husband invited strangers to have sex with her told a court Wednesday he heard her snoring but thought she was "roleplaying."
Richard Wilkins, 62, has pleaded not guilty to rape and assault by penetration in 2016, when he responded to a Craigslist ad by Philip Young to have sex with his then-wife Joanne, who has waived her right to anonymity.
Wilkins and three other men are standing trial at a court in southern England accused of various sexual offences committed jointly with the husband against Joanne Young.
Another man has also admitted similar charges.
Young has admitted multiple counts of drugging and raping her over 13 years.
The court was told he invited men to have sex with her while she was asleep or unconscious, presenting it as a "kink" for the couple.
Wilkins told Winchester Crown Court that he heard a "snoring noise" when he approached a blindfolded and bound Joanne Young in bed.
"I considered this was still part of the role-playing scenario that I was acting out," Wilkins said, adding she stopped snoring when he started having sex with her.
He said he did not suspect that she was drugged or drunk and did not know she was not consenting to the scenario.
Earlier this week, a jury heard statements from another defendant, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, who said Philip Young was a "vile monster" for his actions against his wife.
Sanderson-Doyle, who responded to a Craigslist ad when he was 21 in 2016, said he thought it was a couple who wanted to "fulfil our fantasy."
He said Young was "using pawns in his sick little game."
"I am not stupid and I am not a monster, in hindsight I should have done more," said Sanderson-Doyle, who denies sexual assault by penetration and sexual touching.
The other defendants are Norman Macksoni, 48, accused of rape, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, accused of sexual touching.
The prosecution argued that while the defendants may not have seen Young administer sedatives, they "could patently see its effect."
"They wanted to enact their fantasy and Phil Young's fantasy and they did not care about Jo Young's feelings at all," the prosecution previously told the jury.
There are multiple cases currently before UK courts of alleged drug-facilitated sexual assault, with awareness of the crime growing following the unrelated high-profile 2024 French trial of Dominique Pelicot.
He was found guilty of secretly drugging his wife, Gisele, for years and inviting scores of men to rape her while she was unconscious.
Gisele Pelicot also waived her right to anonymity in that trial to raise awareness about sexual violence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seven foreigners arrested, RM1.08mil worth of drugs seized in Bukit Mertajam
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police arrested seven foreigners and seized suspected methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder and ketamine worth RM1.08 million during raids on two premises in Bukit Tengah here on Nov 1.
Seberang Perai Tengah police chief assistant commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said a team from the district Narcotics Crime Investigation Department raided the premises at 12.50am following surveillance and intelligence gathering.
"Police arrested six men and a woman, all aged between 25 and 38. Inspections of both premises uncovered MDMA powder and ketamine valued at an estimated RM1.08 million," he said in a statement.
Nik Aminuddin said urine screening tests revealed that two of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while the other five tested negative. None of the suspects had prior criminal or drug-related records.
All suspects have been remanded for seven days from Nov 1 to 7 to assist in investigations under Section 39B, Section 12(3), and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act.
Police are continuing investigations to track down the drug syndicate's distribution network.

Title: Elon Musk's business empire braces for Democratic wave as Texas flips blue
Article:
WASHINGTON: As Republicans suffered a landslide defeat and Texas elected its first Democratic governor in more than three decades, one of the biggest losers of the US midterms was not on the ballot: billionaire Elon Musk.
The world's richest man spent nearly half a billion dollars to back Republican candidates and keep Texas red - a state home to his automaker Tesla, rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.
Those bets unravelled as Democrats seized both chambers of Congress and Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, in a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump, a close Musk ally whom the billionaire helped elect.
Musk, who urged his followers on X to vote Republican as recently as Tuesday, now faces a resurgent Democratic Party that he has spent years antagonising.
The GOP's largest donor even threatened retaliation last month on his social media platform after a report said Democrats were considering probes into his companies if they won midterms.
Shares of SpaceX fell 5.5 per cent, while Tesla was down 5.1 per cent as both stocks lagged the broader market.
One of Musk's biggest challenges could be slower approvals for the data centres crucial to tapping the US$28.5 trillion addressable market that SpaceX touted to investors ahead of its IPO.
Analysts and experts expect Democrats to tighten scrutiny of data-centre projects and push for construction moratoriums as local opposition grows over electricity costs.
"A Democratic sweep of Congress would put pressure on tech and potentially bring regulatory pressure on everything AI and possibly slow down the wild, wild west growth figures that we see daily and often take for granted," said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management.
"Musk was the Hail Mary for Republicans leading down to the wire. Unfortunately, his large infusion of cash to back red states could not overcome higher utility bills, prices at the grocery store and prices at the gas pump."
Musk has also drawn scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers over restrictions on satellite communications used by Ukraine's military, mass federal job cuts under his watch at DOGE and the government contracts and subsidies flowing to his companies.
[[nid:1571001]]
One of the lawmakers is Robert Garcia, the next House Oversight Committee chair, who had a blunt two-word message for Republicans and their allies on Tuesday evening: "Lawyer up."
In Texas, Musk also might have to deal with the tenuous relations between him and Hinojosa.
The incoming governor had sued to obtain emails between Musk and Abbott and accused the former governor of selling out the Lone Star state by offering favourable deals to the billionaire.
She has also dismissed Abbott's efforts to rein in data centres as political theater, calling instead for an immediate halt to new projects until lawmakers strengthened protections for local communities, as well as an end to tax breaks.
Musk himself appeared to make light of the hurdles. "Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now," he posted on X, alluding to SpaceX's ambitious plan to put data centres in orbit despite major challenges around cooling and repairs.
The company's AI business is centred around Colossus and Colossus II, two of the world's largest AI data centres near Memphis.
Renting their computing power to customers including Anthropic has sent revenue soaring and helped SpaceX post its first profit as a public company.
But the company aims to nearly double capacity from 1.7 gigawatts at September-end to as much as three gigawatts by year-end, before scaling up to 13 gigawatts next year.
Any delays in bringing the capacity online may hamper Musk's ambitious revenue targets and intensify scrutiny from investors growing wary about AI infrastructure's mounting costs.
Chip research firm SemiAnalysis has identified more than nine gigawatts of planned or developing capacity, including new facilities at SpaceX's Starbase complex in Boca Chica, Texas.
That Boca Chica expansion could face resistance as Hinojosa has opposed the potential sale of a beachfront state park to SpaceX after Texas Monthly reported officials had discussed the deal.
"Let me be clear: Texas is not for sale," Hinojosa said last month.
Musk, meanwhile, has deleted his election-day appeal to his followers to vote Republican.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Democrat El-Sayed hails win amid blue 'tsunami'
Article:
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan's United States Senate race over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
"Michigan, we did it!" said El-Sayed in a speech attended by hundreds of supporters who screamed and hugged each other at his election headquarters in Detroit.
"I am so proud and honoured to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan."
El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curve ball in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour.
The Michigan medical administrator rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal healthcare, to win a key Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.
El-Sayed held a nearly six-point lead on Rogers when networks called the race.
"We are sick and tired of being sick and tired. And I'm so proud of all the work.
"It was boots on the ground. We were always out, but we were never outworked," said party-goer entrepreneur Trunetta Roach, 75, who attended El-Sayed's victory party in downtown Detroit wearing US flag-design diamante high-heels.
"I'm feeling elated. The kids are all right. I was concerned about them. They didn't seem very engaged, but I was wrong. They showed up."
Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.
But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America's fractured, for-profit healthcare system.
"You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill," he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America's divisive multibillion-dollar for-profit medical system.
During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.
El-Sayed also vowed to get "money out of politics" and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo.
The victory made El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969.
"Everybody in politics is so trash. So to see ethical Muslims be at the forefront representing us and showing everybody what we're actually about... it means everything," said micro-influencer Maryam Bozai, 28.
At the victory party, crowds gathered around TVs tuned to left-leaning cable news channel MS NOW, cheering jubilantly each time the Democrat's trademark blue flashed on screen to announce another race won by the party.
"Tsunami! Tsunami!" chanted Ondine Fortune, 64, a Democratic Party media planner.
El-Sayed supporters rubbed shoulders with left-leaning influencers and union activists, a group that lent El-Sayed their formidable campaign infrastructure to reach Michigan's large organised labour community.
Eboni Taylor, a vice-president at Higher Heights which promotes Black women seeking office, said El-Sayed had "gone places where I just would not expect to see him".
"What's most remarkable is that he's showing up in places that are not the usual prescription for the Democratic Party.
"He's going wherever the people want him to be," said Taylor between social media livestreams and celebratory dancing.
El-Sayed faced Islamophobic attacks and mockery for his Arabic name from President Donald Trump and Vice-President JD Vance. But El-Sayed may yet have the last laugh.
Addressing the vice-president, El-Sayed said in his victory speech "you're constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January."
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US midterm voters deliver brutal verdict on Trump
Article:
WASHINGTON: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency.
The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran.
The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump's stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his appointments.
The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump's war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.
"This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back," Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico.
Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results.
"I think the Democrats did a good job," the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. "They fought hard."
But he sought to distance himself from his party's poor showing, adding: "I don't view it as a hit on me."
He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration.
[[nid:1570978]]
Republican heartland
Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine.
In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins.
In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932.
Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008.
In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor's race, ending decades of Republican rule.
Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire.
In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers.
In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024.
Democrats also won Georgia's governorship, electing former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms as the first Black woman governor in US history.
[[nid:1570977]]
Republicans had some consolation in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor and Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat.
But the night was "a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies," George Washington University professor Todd Belt told AFP.
Trump on defensive
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump's MAGA movement "on the run."
Jeffries could become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January.
Trump insisted on social media that Republicans would have won "IN A LANDSLIDE" if he had been running, though he had repeatedly urged supporters throughout the campaign to "pretend I'm on the ballot."
He also repeated his threat to use the presidential veto on Democrat-passed bills, posting a picture on social media of a red baseball cap reading just: "VETO."
On the international front, Russia said it hoped Trump will continue his "peacemaking efforts" and China said it would "continue working" with the United States.
Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, however, said he did not expect the election results to bring about a shift in US policy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Will lame duck Trump cause a flap after the midterms?
Article:
Donald Trump struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone after the Democratic sweep of the United States midterm elections rendered him a lame-duck president. How long that will last is anyone's guess.
From renewed military action against Iran to vetoing Democratic legislation, the volatile 80-year-old could still use his remaining powers to cause major disruption in his last two years in office.
"Every time Trump has been backed into a corner, he has shouted more and come out fighting," said Peter Loge, director of George Washington University's School of Media and Public Affairs.
VETOES AND EXECUTIVE POWER
Trump congratulated the Democrats on Tuesday and said he would be ready to work with them. He may have to, especially if Republicans turn on him over a defeat many of them blame on the Iran war.
But at the same time, Trump repeatedly boasted of his executive power to veto any Democratic legislation that crosses his desk in the Oval Office.
He even posted a picture of a red baseball cap with the word "VETO".
Trump's administration has reportedly drawn up a plan to use executive orders to push through his hardline immigration policies, much as he did in his first 100 days of his second term.
The twice-impeached Trump, the first convicted criminal ever to be elected president, has said he is also ready to fight back against Democratic-led investigations.
WAR WITH IRAN
Foreign policy is the one area in which lame-duck US presidents still have wide-ranging powers.
Trump may renew large-scale military operations against Iran, although he indicated on Tuesday that he was still seeking a deal to end the war he launched in February.
"Otherwise I'll just finish the job," he told Fox News.
"I don't think he wants his legacy to be a warmonger. He wants his legacy to have left America stronger," said Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution.
Trump also dismissed speculation that he could fire Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth as the Iran war drags on, as part of a cabinet reshuffle.
UKRAINE, DETENTE AND TRADE
Trump has long wanted to be seen as a peacemaker and is likely to continue to push Ukraine to agree to a settlement with Russia.
Fresh trilateral talks are set for next week.
But Trump's leverage with the leaders he views as his great power equals —Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin — may be hit by his midterms defeat.
The election hammering comes less than two weeks before the three could potentially meet at a summit in China later this month.
MONUMENTS TO HIMSELF
Trump may, however, choose to step back from confrontation and focus on his favourite subject — stamping his physical legacy on Washington.
In his closing midterms speech, Trump barely mentioned policy and instead talked about his renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other plans to beautify Washington.
His pride and joy is the giant US$400 million ballroom that he is building at the White House, and which is due to be completed in late 2028 — shortly before he leaves office for good.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China seeks arrest of five Uyghurs held in Thailand
Article:
BANGKOK: Five Uyghurs detained in Thailand since 2014 are subject to Chinese arrest warrants, the kingdom's security chief said Wednesday, adding that a court would decide if they would be returned to China.
Human rights groups have raised concerns about the men – members of the Muslim minority group who activists say are persecuted in China – after two of them were pardoned by Thailand last month.
They were among more than 300 Uyghurs held in Thailand in 2014, most of whom have since left – including a group of around 40 sent last year to China, a move that sparked international outrage.
The five were jailed for trying to escape immigration detention in 2020 and under Thai law have to serve their sentences before deportation.
Two of them were pardoned last month and are in immigration detention awaiting their fate.
"These five have arrest warrants in China and they have no refugee status," Chaipruak Doungprapat, secretary-general of Thailand's National Security Council, told reporters on Wednesday.
He said that if China requests their extradition, Thailand's foreign ministry would make an assessment and a court would then decide.
"If the court rules that they are guilty, they will be handed over under the extradition treaty," Chaipruak said.
"If they win, it depends on whether any (other) country is willing to take them."
Asked Wednesday about the fate of the five men, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning did not provide details.
"China and Thailand's cooperation in combating cross-border criminal activities such as illegal immigration is in line with the two countries' laws, international law and international practice," she said.
'GRAVE RISKS'
Thailand is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention, but is bound by the international legal principle of non-refoulement, which bars countries from sending people back to places where their lives or freedom are in danger.
Human Rights Watch warned Wednesday that the Uyghurs faced "grave risks of torture and other serious abuses" in China, and should be allowed to travel to a safe third country.
Beijing has been accused of detaining more than a million Uyghurs and other Muslims since 2017, part of a campaign that the United Nations previously said could constitute crimes against humanity.
China vehemently denies these allegations, saying its policies have boosted economic development and rooted out extremism in the Xinjiang region, where most Uyghurs are from.
In letters written by the two pardoned men and shared with AFP by Peace Rights Foundation, which provides them legal representation, they said they do not want to return to China.
"If we go back to China, we and our parents must receive death sentence(s)," one letter says.
"The Uyghur people have no human rights and are treated lower than animals."
It adds: "China is slandering us. We aren't terrorist(s)."
'RATHER DIE'
Thailand's foreign ministry did not immediately reply to emailed questions from AFP.
But a ministry official told a parliament committee on September 16 that both China and a Western country had requested five detained Uyghurs be sent to them, according to parliamentary minutes.
Kannavee Suebsang, chairman of Peace Rights Foundation, said defence lawyers have not been given access to the two pardoned men since October 21 when they were moved to immigration custody.
The pair told a Thai human rights commissioner on Wednesday that they want to be resettled in a third country, Kannavee told AFP.
"They refuse to return to China and would rather die first."

Title: NST Leader: A lesson from Penang
Article:
The 1993 Highland Towers tragedy claimed 48 lives. The incident prompted greater attention to regulations governing hillside development, slope maintenance and disaster-response coordination.
Recurring concerns surrounding hillside development in Penang serve as a reminder that the lessons of Highland Towers must never be forgotten. For four decades, residents and civil society groups have raised objections to high-density projects on the island's steep and environmentally sensitive slopes.
These concerns date back to the late 1980s and gained renewed prominence in 2007, when opposition mounted against the proposed RM25 billion Penang Global City Centre at the Penang Turf Club site.
Over the years, planning guidelines and restrictions have been introduced to address the challenges of hillside development, including provisions in the Penang Structure Plan relating to slopes above 76m or with gradients exceeding 25 degrees.
However, concerns have persisted, particularly over the balance between development needs and environmental and public safety considerations.
Penang has experienced several devastating landslides. In 2017, a landslide at the Granito construction site in Tanjung Bungah claimed 11 lives.
A year later, the Bukit Kukus landslide, during hill-clearing works, killed nine workers. The latest tragedy in Paya Terubong last month, which claimed the life of 73-year-old retired doctor Dr Wong Kar Lin, has once again brought these concerns into sharp focus.
Dr Wong was among those who voiced concerns about hillside development. Penang's limited supply of flat, developable land, coupled with strong demand for housing and infrastructure, has inevitably placed greater attention on alternative development sites.
Hillside land also presents different land acquisition and development cost considerations. These competing priorities make it all the more important that safety remains paramount at every stage of the planning and development process.
Following the latest tragedy, residents and civil society groups have called for a State Commission of Inquiry and a white paper to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify lessons to be drawn.
A transparent and comprehensive examination would help address public concerns, establish responsibility and strengthen confidence in the processes governing hillside development. Penang's experience should serve as a reminder to other states.
Ultimately, planners, developers and the authorities must ensure every hillside project is supported by rigorous geological assessments, proper slope stabilisation measures and effective drainage systems.
These safeguards must continue beyond planning approval, with regular monitoring, maintenance and compliance throughout construction and after completion.
Economic progress is necessary, but it must never come at the expense of public safety, environmental sustainability or the quality of life of existing communities. The consequences of getting it wrong are simply too grave.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK parliament risks 'catastrophic failure' over delayed renovation
Article:
LONDON: Britain's centuries-old parliament is at risk of a "Notre Dame-like" fire or other catastrophe if lawmakers continue to put off a major restoration project, MPs warned Wednesday.
Crumbling masonry, ageing electrics, frequent leaks and high asbestos levels are some of the problems besetting the Palace of Westminster, parts of which are over 900 years old.
Billions of pounds are required to renovate the estate, which sits within a Unesco world heritage site, but parliamentarians have been unable to decide for years on how to proceed.
Parliament's public accounts committee said the delay was leading to spiralling costs and risked causing a "catastrophic failure" that would harm the UK's "morale and reputation."
"A lack of action risks, for instance, the chamber being plunged into darkness during the state opening of parliament," said chair Geoffrey Clifton-Brown MP, referencing when the monarch comes to the lower House of Commons to read out the government's legislation plans.
"Consider the impact of global rolling news footage of Notre Dame-like flames licking out of the building's roof, resulting in the destruction of our heritage, or worse, injuries or loss of life.
"These are not notional possibilities, but real and rising risks," he added.
Most of the central London site, including the internationally recognised Elizabeth Tower commonly known as Big Ben, was built during the 1800s when Queen Victoria was on the throne.
Parliamentarians first voted to move out of the central London site in 2018 to allow extensive repairs. But there has since been disagreement about whether this should go ahead.
A series of votes is expected in both the House of Commons and the upper House of Lords chamber on the so-called Restoration and Renewal programme later this year.
The current options include a "full decant" costing up to £15.6 billion and lasting up to 24 years, where both houses leave for much of the works.
A partial decant called "enhanced maintenance and improvement plus" where no more than 30 percent of staff would stay on site at any one time is projected to cost £39 billion and take up to 61 years.
Current timescales predict that work would start in 2032.
In its report, the committee warned that the weekly cost of maintenance on the parliamentary estate is expected to grow from the current £1.5 million to £2 million in coming years.
Each year the programme is delayed will add £420 million to the lifetime costs of delivering the scheme, it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Transport Ministry working to resolve train congestion, technical issues, says Loke
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The Transport Ministry is working to address train service congestion and resolve technical issues faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
"Rapid KL is working to address various technical challenges. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service," he said.
He told reporters this after the ministry's get-together with Tamil media practitioners at Tropicana Golf and Country Resort.
On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public's daily routine.
The directive followed a complaint by a Threads user to Anwar about overcrowding at train stations.
Meanwhile, Loke said train frequencies were increased during the festive season to encourage more people to use public transport when returning to their hometowns.
He said Electric Train Service (ETS) trips from Kuala Lumpur to states along the west coast, including Kedah and Johor, had received an encouraging response, with additional services scheduled ahead of Deepavali.
"We have added trips ahead of Deepavali, and Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is working to ensure service frequency is increased so that more people can take the train home," he said.
Earlier, Loke said the event served as a platform to strengthen ties between the ministry and Tamil media practitioners in conjunction with Deepavali.
He said the media played an important role in disseminating information on the ministry's policies and services to all segments of society, including the Indian community.
Close cooperation with media practitioners was also essential to ensure clear communication on road safety, public transport, the Road Transport Department and the aviation sector, he added.

Title: Country Heights property auction draws no bidders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Country Heights Holdings Bhd's latest public auction of its property in Petaling Jaya has failed to attract bidders.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the public auction of the property belonging to Mines Waterfront Business Park Sdn Bhd was unsuccessful due to the absence of bidders.
MBSB Bank Bhd initiated the auction, which took place on Wednesday at 9am via the e-Lelong platform.
The auction proceeded pursuant to an order for sale issued by the High Court of Malaya at Shah Alam.
The leasehold land spans 667,147 square feet and had a reserve price of RM152.77 million.
Country Heights' shares closed one sen or 7.69 per cent higher at 14 sen, valuing the company at RM45.61 million.

Title: Dollar and oil drop after Trump's election rout
Article:
LONDON: The dollar and oil prices dropped on Wednesday as traders digested President Donald Trump's heavy defeat in US midterm elections that saw his Republican party lose control of Congress.
Democrats seized control of both houses in a landslide victory that gives them the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.
"Investors are trying to get their heads around what a Democrat landslide means for financial markets," noted Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.
"The big risk is uncertainty around how Trump could act in the coming months following such a result."
The dollar sank against other major currencies on fears the vote outcome could lead to US political gridlock, after Trump warned that he would become "Mr Veto."
Technology firms also slumped amid suggestions Democrats could prioritise AI regulation.
But European stock markets posted gains in Wednesday morning trading.
London, Frankfurt and Paris all rose by more than one percent – investors brushing off official data showing eurozone inflation reaching a three-year high of 4.0 per cent.
That followed a largely solid performance by equities across Asia, though Tokyo ended lower as its tech sector struggled.
Tens of millions of Americans voted in the crucial polls pitched as a referendum on the White House, as anger grows at surging petrol prices, the impact of tariffs and the Iran war.
Chris Weston, analyst at broker Pepperstone, stressed that Trump retained "considerable executive authority" so the possible impact was "far from straightforward."
Bond yields avoided the volatility seen recently, while gold benefitted from its status as a safe haven investment.
Aside from the US vote, investors continued to follow third-quarter earnings.
BMW said Wednesday it would step up planned job cuts as it reported a drop in third-quarter profit, hit by cutthroat competition and falling demand in China, the world's largest car market.
Google meanwhile said it planned to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure.

Title: Nga: Govt saves RM3bil by leasing 28 helicopters
Article:
SUBANG: The government has saved RM3 billion through a leasing arrangement for 28 helicopters for use by various government agencies, including two AW139 units that have expanded the Fire and Rescue Department's fleet to 10 helicopters.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the leasing arrangement, instead of direct purchases, shifted maintenance responsibilities to the leasing company throughout the 15-year contract period.
"Before this, we had to buy (helicopters). Now, we have a leasing system and we are now maintenance-free," he said at the launch of the Fire and Rescue Department AW139 helicopter operations.
He said the two AW139 helicopters would strengthen the department's capabilities in search and rescue (SAR) operations, forest firefighting and the delivery of logistical aid.
"Before the addition of the two AW139s, the department operated eight helicopters strategically placed at three air bases in Penang, Selangor and Sarawak.
"The department also has 26 helicopter pilots, including qualified flight instructors for the AW109 and AW139 helicopters to support its smooth operation," Nga said.
Nga added that aviation safety must continue to be a priority, alongside strengthening cooperation between agencies and the industry in the development of aviation technology, training and expertise building.
Also present at the event were Housing and Local Government Ministry secretary-general Datuk Wira Dr M Noor Azman Taib, Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad, Weststar Group managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim, and the Italian Ambassador to Malaysia, Raffaele Langella.

Title: Abang Johari given full mandate to decide on GPS candidates, says Uggah
Article:
KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg has been given full mandate to decide on the coalition's candidates for the 13th Sarawak election.
Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) deputy president, who is also Sarawak Deputy Premier, Datuk Douglas Uggah Embas said the agreement was reached by all GPS component parties in a coalition meeting.
"Everyone agreed and supported giving Abang Johari the mandate to make the final decision on candidate selection," he told reporters after attending a PBB Supreme Working Council meeting.
On Oct 23, Abang Johari, who is also Sarawak Premier, announced that the Sarawak state legislative assembly would be dissolved effective Oct 26.
The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on Nov 6 to discuss key dates and other matters related to the state election.
GPS comprises four component parties, namely PBB, Parti Rakyat Bersatu Sarawak (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Parti Demokratik Progresif (PDP).
Meanwhile, commenting on the possibility of the state election being held during the northeast ,onsoon, Uggah said the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee would liaise with the EC for monitoring and coordination based on the latest weather forecasts.
"We do not yet know when the election will be held, but we have been informed that the monsoon season has begun and will continue until March next year," he said.

Title: Indonesia to push for ratification of Asean haze centre agreement
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia will push for the ratification of an agreement to operationalise the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACCTHPC) at the 49th Asean Summit in Manila.
Foreign Ministry Director-General for Asean Cooperation Ina Krisnamurthi said the centre already had a secretariat in Jakarta but could not begin operations until Asean member states ratified the agreement.
She said at least six member states must ratify the agreement before it can take effect, but so far only Vietnam has completed the process.
"The centre must be up and running. Otherwise, there is no point in establishing a centre that cannot function. We must immediately implement what we have envisioned through this centre," she said on Wednesday, according to Antara news agency.
Ina described the centre as a potential game changer in strengthening the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP), which came into force in 2003.
"The centre will be a game changer, strengthening the agreement Asean established in 2003, followed by the monitoring system Indonesia pushed for in 2013. We continued to push for it again in 2023," she said.

Title: CAAM: Helicopter landed in Bintulu as precautionary measure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Reports that a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter had to make an emergency landing in Bintulu were inaccurate.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the pilot made the landing as a precautionary measure.
This was confirmed by the aircraft operator, Layang Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, which also said the helicopter was not operating under the FDS nor as a medical evacuation (medevac) flight at the time.
Norazman said the pilot landed the helicopter near the Sri Pertiwi housing estate in Kidurong, Bintulu, at 3.18pm.
"I can confirm that the pilot made a precautionary landing and that the pilot did not declare an emergency. The pilot and two passengers are safe," he said.
Earlier, it was reported that a helicopter was seen making what was believed to be an
emergency landing
near the housing estate.
The incident went viral after a 51-second video showing the helicopter landing in an open area circulated on social media.
LLASB, in a statement, said the helicopter was undertaking a repositioning flight, adding that the two "passengers" on board were actually technicians.
A repositioning flight is the term used when an aircraft is flown from one location to another, usually without commercial passengers aboard.
LLASB accountable manager Captain Shahdon Poong said the pilot of helicopter, registered as 9M-LLE, had notified Bintulu Air Traffic Control of the situation at the time of the landing.
"Following the landing, the pilot requested the company's mobile engineering response team to inspect the aircraft and conduct the necessary technical assessments.
"LLASB places the highest priority on aviation safety and remains committed to ensuring that all operational and technical procedures are conducted in accordance with applicable aviation safety standards," it said.
The company said it would issue a further statement tomorrow following a review of the engineering team's findings.

Title: MMEA investigating collision between local boat and unidentified vessel
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) is conducting further investigations into an incident involving a local fishing boat that was struck by another vessel in Terengganu waters.
Terengganu Maritime director Captain Hamiludin Che Awang said based on a witness account, the incident occurred around 5am, approximately 33 nautical miles from the Kuala Terengganu estuary.
The local Class A fishing boat was drifting at the time, while its five crew members, including the skipper, were resting.
"One of the crew members later noticed a much larger boat approaching at high speed before a collision occurred, damaging the rear section and roof structure of the local fishing boat.
"The vessel involved in the collision left the scene. None of the local fishing boat's crew members was injured," he said.
Hamiludin said the fishing boat was later brought back to Duyong Jetty for repairs, with its owner estimating the damage to be about RM10,000.
He said a report was lodged to facilitate further investigations.
The identity of the vessel involved in the collision has yet to be established.
"A check of previous arrest records at the Terengganu MMEA headquarters also found no record of Vietnamese fishing boats being detained in the area, approximately 33 nautical miles from Kuala Terengganu, as alleged in connection with the incident.
"As such, the public is urged not to speculate or spread unverified information while investigations are ongoing," he said.

Title: Aliff Daniel ordered to undergo three-month faith rehabilitation over improper worship
Article:
RAWANG: A 21-year-old man who went viral for performing religious rituals at a temple in Batu Caves has been ordered to undergo three months of faith rehabilitation after pleading guilty to a charge of improper worship.
The Syariah Lower Court ordered Aliff Daniel Adli to undergo rehabilitation at the Baitul Iman Faith Rehabilitation Centre in Ulu Yam, beginning today.
Syariah judge Mohd Faizal Habib made the order under Section 54(1) of the Selangor Syariah Criminal Offences Enactment 1995, which allows the court to substitute imprisonment and fines with rehabilitation at an approved centre for up to six months.
Aliff was charged with committing improper worship by holding up a religious object, performing a ritual involving body piercing and kneeling with both hands clasped against his chest in front of a statue.
The offence occurred at a temple in Batu Caves, between 9pm and 11pm on Jan 24, 2024.
The charge was framed under Section 4(1) of the same enactment, which provides for a fine of up to RM3,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
In his ruling, Faizal said the offence was not merely a breach of written law but a serious transgression involving syirik (associating partners with Allah).
"The offence you committed is not merely an ordinary criminal offence. More than that, it involves your faith and tauhid as a Muslim.
"At the age of 18 when you committed the offence, perhaps you were exploring various things as a young person, but you must understand that there are limits.
"Although you have said that you have repented, this court advises you to truly repent through taubat nasuha," he said.
Faizal said the court took into account Aliff's young age and his responsibility towards his mother, who had recently undergone surgery.
"Taking into account your young age and to ensure that you can look after yourself as well as your mother, whom you emphasised during mitigation, the court orders you to undergo rehabilitation at the Baitul Iman Faith Rehabilitation Centre for three months, beginning today," he said.
Aliff, dressed in a white shirt and kopiah, was subsequently escorted to the centre by Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) officers.
Earlier, Syarie prosecutor Zamniazura Mohd Sarin urged the court to exercise its discretionary powers under Section 54(1) and replace the usual penalties with a rehabilitation order.
In his mitigation, Aliff, who is unemployed, appealed for a minimum fine instead of imprisonment, saying he needed to care for his mother, who had recently undergone surgery.
He also told the court that he had repented and sought permission to attend religious guidance classes at a mosque near his home.
"I also seek permission to attend religious guidance classes at a mosque near my home," he said.
However, the prosecution objected, arguing that he needed to be monitored by religious authorities at a rehabilitation centre.
The prosecution was conducted by Siti Nor Hashibah Jamhari, Zamniazura and Husaini Roslin, while Aliff was unrepresented.
The court fixed Feb 25 next year for mention for the prosecution to update it on his rehabilitation progress.

Title: One dead, two missing after Indonesian army helicopter crash during firefighting operations
Article:
JAKARTA: One person was killed and two others remain missing after a Mi-17V5 helicopter belonging to the Indonesian Army crashed while conducting a forest firefighting operation in Central Kalimantan on Wednesday.
The army's information department said the helicopter, carrying eight crew members, crashed into the waters of the Perlu River in Lake Sembuluh, Seruyan, around 11.18am local time while conducting a firefighting operation in Tanjung Puting National Park.
The helicopter departed from Kuala Pembuang at 9.55 am towards Telaga Pulang before crashing while collecting water for a water bombing operation.
The helicopter departed from Kuala Pembuang at 9.55am for Telaga Pulang before crashing while collecting water for a water-bombing operation.
"One crew member died and his remains have been brought to Kuala Pembuang Hospital, while five others were successfully rescued and are now receiving treatment at the same hospital.
"Two more crew members are still missing. A search and rescue operation by a joint team is underway in the air and water," the department said in a statement.
The cause of the crash is still under investigation.

Title: Mercedes-Benz C-Class goes electric, priced from RM360,888
Article:
MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has opened pre-bookings for the all-new electric C-Class, with the C 300 4Matic electric AMG Line Plus carrying an estimated price starting from RM360,888.
The electric saloon is the first fully electric version of the German marque's C-Class, one of its established model lines.
The model has a claimed driving range of up to 690km under the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP), supported by an 85kWh battery and 800-volt electrical architecture.
It supports DC fast charging at up to 320kW, allowing up to 290km of range to be added in 10 minutes under suitable charging conditions.
An optional 22kW-capable onboard AC charging system is also available.
The dual-motor 4Matic all-wheel-drive system produces a combined output of 310kW and 800Nm of torque, enabling acceleration from zero to 100kph in 4.5 seconds.
The vehicle also features a two-speed transmission on the rear axle, designed to balance acceleration and efficiency at higher speeds.
Inside, the electric C-Class features a 39.1-inch MBUX Hyperscreen stretching across the dashboard, alongside a panoramic roof with 162 illuminated stars and a 470-litre boot.
A front storage compartment provides an additional 101 litres of capacity.
Safety and driver assistance features include up to 27 cameras and sensors, parking assistance with a 360-degree view and up to 11 airbags.
Mercedes-Benz Malaysia chief executive officer and president Martin Schulz said the introduction gives local customers an electric alternative while retaining the C-Class's established characteristics.
The model is also offered under the company's Agility+ financing programme, with estimated monthly payments starting from RM3,988, subject to prevailing interest rates and terms and conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt to conduct cyber threat stress tests across sectors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will conduct a series of stress tests across various sectors to assess the country's preparedness against cyber threats, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would also provide an early warning system capable of broadcasting official government information directly to mobile phones nationwide.
"Its original purpose was to notify the public of localised disasters, but it can also serve as a nationwide broadcast system pushing official government information directly to mobile phones.
"These are among the matters being examined by the National Security Council and the Communications Ministry itself," he told reporters at the Mega Bazaar Deepavali 2026.
Asked about the rollout, Fahmi said he would check its latest status to determine whether it could be expedited.
He said the ministry was also tasked with assessing cybersecurity across the country's telecommunications and broadcasting networks, including those operated by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) and Bernama.
The move follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive for Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and the National Security Council to assess the country's preparedness against cyber threats.
Fahmi said several agencies, including Bank Negara Malaysia, MCMC, the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, had been convened to review the country's readiness against hybrid attacks.
These include threats from non-state actors exploiting technologies such as artificial intelligence to hack systems and disrupt domestic supply chains.
Earlier, Anwar said Malaysia was among the countries considered
potential targets of cyberattacks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sunway Construction's unit clinches RM920mil variation works contract in Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd's wholly owned unit Sunway Construction Sdn Bhd has received a letter of award for variation (LOAV) works from a US-headquartered multinational technology corporation worth approximately RM920.8 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the construction group said the variation works involve additional mechanical, electrical, and plumbing fit-out works for the ongoing development of a data centre in Johor.
"The LOAV also serves as the instruction to commence the variation works, which are targeted to be completed by the first quarter in 2028 (Q1 2028)," it said.
The group said the variation works contract will not affect the group's share capital or substantial shareholders' shareholdings, as no new shares will be allotted or issued under the variation works.
"The variation works are not expected to have any immediate material effect on the earnings per share, net assets per share and gearing of the group for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
"However, barring any unforeseen circumstances, the variation works are expected to contribute positively to the earnings of the group for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, onwards," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FDS still grounded amid reports of helicopter's emergency landing in Bintulu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in Sarawak has yet to resume operations and is still undergoing further scrutiny and assessment before any decision is made on its reactivation.
The Health Ministry said any resumption of the service would have to take into account operational safety, the welfare of personnel and staff readiness.
"The Health Ministry emphasises that the FDS in Sarawak has yet to resume operations and is still undergoing further scrutiny and assessment before any decision is made on its reactivation.
"Any resumption of the service must take into account operational safety, the welfare of personnel and staff readiness," it said when contacted.
This comes after a
helicopter was seen
making an emergency landing in Bintulu today following a minor technical problem while travelling from Sibu to Miri, according to a report by Borneo Post.
Bintulu police chief Superintendent Nixon Joshua Ali said the helicopter was heading to Miri to take part in an exhibition programme when the incident occurred around 3.20pm.
"The helicopter made an emergency landing due to a minor technical problem. There were no Health Ministry passengers, only the pilot and two crew members," he told the regional paper.
The incident went viral after a 51-second video showing the helicopter landing in an open area near the housing estate circulated on social media.
The video, uploaded to the Bintulu News Page 2 Facebook page, showed the helicopter on an open field next to the housing estate.
The FDS suspension followed a
helicopter crash in Long Lellang
, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8, which killed all five people on board.
The BO-105 helicopter, bearing registration number 9M-LLF, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) port around 3.40pm while carrying a pilot and four Health Ministry personnel.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
Following the tragedy, the Health Ministry
suspended all FDS operations
in Sarawak to allow investigations and a reassessment of the service's safety aspects and operational mechanisms.
It is understood that the helicopter's operator would be issuing a statement.

Title: 1,500 oil palm smallholders to benefit from replanting financing incentive scheme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,500 independent smallholders, covering 5,900ha, are expected to benefit from the Smallholder Oil Palm Replanting Financing Incentive Scheme (TSPKS) 2.0 under the 2027 Budget.
Plantations and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said the programme aims to support independent smallholders in replanting activities and strengthen the sustainability of the oil palm sector.
"In addition, 740 independent oil palm smallholders, with a combined cultivation area of 11,110 hectares, are expected to benefit from the Oil Palm Replanting Financing Programme (PTSS)," she said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in Dewan Rakyat today.
Under the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an allocation of RM200 million for TSPKS 2.0.
The government will also continue the PTSS, which provides financial assistance to eligible smallholders facing capital constraints.
Meanwhile, on the income of rubber smallholders, Noraini said that their actual earnings were influenced by production levels, including tapping frequency and the size of their plantations.
"The ministry will continue to maintain the rubber production incentive (IPG) as an income-guarantee mechanism based on the activation pricing level (PHP).
"Smallholders will benefit from the IPG, particularly when prices fall below the PHP threshold," she said, adding that the IPG price threshold had been increased seven times since 2015.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: No instructions from Bersatu to supporters to back PH
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu has not issued any instructions to its grassroots members to support Pakatan Harapan candidates in seats where there is no contest between the two coalitions in the Melaka election.
Its vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu said although the party had not issued any instructions to its members and supporters, it appreciated PH's willingness to support its candidates.
"Although (Melaka Pakatan Harapan chairman) Adly Zahari had stated openly that his side had no objection to supporting us in seats it is not contesting, we have not issued any instructions on our part.
"At the same time, however, we are grateful that PH leaders have expressed such a willingness," he said when met while campaigning in the Ayer Keroh constituency here.
Adly had previously said the coalition had
no objection
to its supporters backing Bersatu candidates in state seats it was not contesting.
He was reported to have said that although there was no formal cooperation between PH and Bersatu, the approach was intended to minimise clashes with the party led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, while allowing such support to take place.
In a separate development, Ahmad Faizal said Bersatu was hopeful of retaining the two seats it won in the 2021 state election, namely Sungai Udang and Bemban.
He said the target was realistic, based on the preparations made by the party's machinery at all levels.
"Based on what we can see in terms of the machinery's preparations and other factors, I hope securing two or three seats is not impossible.
"If we thought we would get the same result (as in Negri Sembilan), I do not think we would have fielded candidates.
"However, if the results do not go our way, we will continue to strive. Our struggle does not end with the Melaka election," he said.
In the 2021 Melaka election, Bersatu won two seats, namely Sungai Udang and Bemban.
This time, the party is contesting seven seats, compared with its initial plan to field candidates in eight, after making way for Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia in Gadek.
On its last-minute decision to withdraw from the contest in Gadek, Ahmad Faizal said it was made because coordination issues could not be resolved in time.
"The decision was made after taking into account the preparations of the party machinery and the readiness of our ally to contest in the constituency.
"We have also asked our members and supporters in Gadek to support the Putra candidate as part of the cooperation between the two parties under the Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR) coalition," he said.
Asked whether the Melaka election could serve as a test for more formal cooperation between PH and Bersatu ahead of future elections, Ahmad Faizal said his party was open to discussions with any party that shared similar ideals and objectives.
Meanwhile, he said Bersatu still regarded itself as part of Perikatan Nasional, despite statements by several coalition leaders questioning the party's position.
This follows the issue surrounding the cancellation of PN's registration by the Registrar of Societies (ROS).
He said that, based on his understanding of the PN constitution, Bersatu remained part of the coalition, and any differences of opinion should be resolved through discussions and negotiations between the party leaderships.
